InventLock in main, unlock in another thread

    

      
void T_worker(int tid) {

      
    tid--;

      
    for (int i = 0; i < LENGTH(edges); i++)

      
        if (edges[i].dst == tid) mutex_lock(&edges[i].lk);

      
    printf("Computing node #%d...\n", tid);

      
    sleep(1);

      
    for (int i = 0; i < LENGTH(edges); i++)

      
        if (edges[i].src == tid) mutex_unlock(&edges[i].lk);

      
}

      
int main() {

      
    for (int i = 0; i < LENGTH(edges); i++) {

      
        mutex_init(&edges[i].lk);

      
        mutex_lock(&edges[i].lk);

      
    }

      
    for (int i = 0; i < NTASKS; i++) spawn(T_worker);

      
    join();

      
}

InventYou just invented the semaphore

    

      
void P(sem_t *sem) {     // take a key

      
    mutex_lock(&sem->lk);

      
    while (!(sem->count > 0))

      
        cond_wait(&sem->cv, &sem->lk);

      
    sem->count--;

      
    mutex_unlock(&sem->lk);

      
}

      
void V(sem_t *sem) {     // put a key back

      
    mutex_lock(&sem->lk);

      
    sem->count++;

      
    cond_broadcast(&sem->cv);

      
    mutex_unlock(&sem->lk);

      
}

OrderA lock is a semaphore with one key

    

      
sem_t sem;

      
void lock()   { P(&sem); }

      
void unlock() { V(&sem); }

      
void T_sum() {

      
    for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {

      
        lock();

      
        sum++;

      
        unlock();

      
    }

      
}

      
int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {

      
    SEM_INIT(&sem, 1);

      
    if (argc > 1)

      
        unlock();   // the bug: one unlock() too many

      
    spawn(T_sum); spawn(T_sum); join();

      
}

Orderjoin: one table per thread

    

      
sem_t done[16];

      
void worker_init(int T) {

      
    count = T;

      
    for (int i = 1; i <= T; i++) SEM_INIT(&done[i], 0);

      
}

      
void worker_done(int id) {

      
    V(&done[id]);

      
}

      
void worker_join() {

      
    for (int i = 1; i <= count; i++) P(&done[i]);

      
}

      
void T_worker(int id) {   // join-main.c

      
    printf("Thread %d start.\n", id); sleep(1);

      
    printf("Thread %d end.\n", id);

      
    worker_done(id);

      
}

OrderAny graph: one semaphore per node

    

      
sem_t vertex_sem[NTASKS];

      
void T_worker(int tid) {

      
    tid--;

      
    for (int i = 0; i < LENGTH(edges); i++)

      
        if (edges[i].dst == tid) P(&vertex_sem[tid]);

      
    printf("Computing node #%d...\n", tid);

      
    sleep(1);

      
    for (int i = 0; i < LENGTH(edges); i++)

      
        if (edges[i].src == tid) V(&vertex_sem[edges[i].dst]);

      
}

      
int main() {

      
    for (int i = 0; i < NTASKS; i++) SEM_INIT(&vertex_sem[i], 0);

      
    for (int i = 0; i < NTASKS; i++) spawn(T_worker);

      
    join();

      
}

BufferProducer-consumer in six lines

    

      
sem_t fill, empty;

      
void T_produce() {

      
    while (1) {

      
        P(&empty);      // need an empty slot

      
        printf("(");

      
        V(&fill);       // make a filled slot

      
    }

      
}

      
void T_consume() {

      
    while (1) {

      
        P(&fill);       // need a filled slot

      
        printf(")");

      
        V(&empty);      // make an empty slot

      
    }

      
}

ForksWith a CV: write the condition down

    

      
void T_philosopher(int id) {

      
    int lhs = (id + N - 1) % N, rhs = id % N;

      
    while (1) {

      
        mutex_lock(&lk);

      
        while (!(avail[lhs] && avail[rhs]))

      
            cond_wait(&cv, &lk);

      
        avail[lhs] = avail[rhs] = 0;  // take both at once

      
        mutex_unlock(&lk);

      
        // eat: print "+ lhs", "+ rhs", "- lhs", "- rhs"

      
        mutex_lock(&lk);

      
        avail[lhs] = avail[rhs] = 1;  // put both back

      
        cond_broadcast(&cv);          // everyone checks again

      
        mutex_unlock(&lk);

      
    }

      
}

ForksOne semaphore per fork: all take the left

    

      
sem_t avail[N];   // SEM_INIT(&avail[i], 1): one key per fork

      
void T_philosopher(int id) {

      
    int lhs = (id + N - 1) % N;

      
    int rhs = id % N;

      
    while (1) {

      
        P(&avail[lhs]);

      
        printf("+ %d by T%d\n", lhs, id);

      
        P(&avail[rhs]);

      
        printf("+ %d by T%d\n", rhs, id);

      
        // eat: print "- lhs", "- rhs"

      
        V(&avail[lhs]);

      
        V(&avail[rhs]);

      
    }

      
}

HarderA condition variable from semaphores?

    

      
void wait(cond_t *cv, mutex_t *mutex) {

      
    cv->nwait++;

      
    mutex_unlock(mutex);

      
    P(&cv->sleep);

      
    mutex_lock(mutex);

      
}

      
void broadcast(cond_t *cv) {

      
    mutex_lock(&cv->lock);

      
    for (int i = 0; i < cv->nwait; i++)

      
        V(&cv->sleep);

      
    cv->nwait = 0;

      
    mutex_unlock(&cv->lock);

      
}

    

    

    
nwait = 0

    
sleep: 0 

    

    

    
"Implementing condition variables out of a simple primitive like semaphores is surprisingly tricky."Andrew Birrell, Microsoft Research, 2003 · the real fix: unlock-and-sleep as one step, with the kernel's help (futex)

    
Unlock and sleep must be one step; semaphores alone cannot give it

    
wait() and broadcast() as in the source lecture · A. Birrell, "Implementing Condition Variables with Semaphores", Microsoft Research Silicon Valley, January 2003 · schedule chosen to show the lost wake-up

  

  

    

    
WaiterHire a waiter: one thread owns the forks

    

      
void T_philosopher(int id) {

      
    while (1) {

      
        send(id);  P(&can_eat[id]);    // ask, then wait for "yes"

      
        /* eat */  send(-id);            // give the forks back

      
} }

      
void T_waiter() {

      
    int fork_free[N] = {1, 1, 1, 1, 1};   // only the waiter: no lock

      
    while (1) {

      
        int req = receive();

      
        int id = req > 0 ? req : -req;

      
        if (req < 0)

      
            fork_free[(id + N - 1) % N] = fork_free[id % N] = 1;

      
        else pending[np++] = id;

      
        for (int i = 0; i < np; i++) {        // oldest first

      
            int p = pending[i], l = (p + N - 1) % N, r = p % N;

      
            if (fork_free[l] && fork_free[r]) {

      
                fork_free[l] = fork_free[r] = 0;

      
                V(&can_eat[p]);           // p leaves pending

      
} } } }
